To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the epidemiology of DENV infection in Nha Trang, Vietnam, is characterized by pronounced interannual and spatial variation in dengue incidence, with a high proportion of the population having evidence of previous DENV infection, and that mobility patterns of the population are characterized by a high proportion of daytime hours spent within a short distance of home.

we have conducted a series of studies in Nha Trang, Vietnam, which have characterized the epidemiology of DENV infection, and the population mobility patterns of children in this setting, in order to inform the design of future trials to test the effectiveness of community level dengue preventive measures.

we conducted a series of epidemiological, serological, and virological studies to characterize dengue in Nha Trang, Vietnam, and identified children 7 years of age, children and young adults, and substantial spatial and temporal heterogeneity of dengue as optimal targets for future intervention studies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the epidemiology of DENV in Nha Trang city and how it varies over time.
the epidemiology of infectious diseases in Vietnam.
understanding the epidemiology of DENV in Nha Trang, Vietnam, with particular reference to spatial and temporal heterogeneity.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we conducted a series of prospective and retrospective studies to characterize the population mobility patterns and dengue epidemiology in Nha Trang, Vietnam, with the aim of informing the design of a future dengue prevention trial.
the epidemiology of DENV in Nha Trang is complex, with pronounced interannual and spatial variability.
we have shown that dengue is a significant public health burden in Nha Trang, with pronounced interannual and spatial variability in dengue transmission.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the design of a trial of a community based intervention for dengue prevention in Vietnam requires careful consideration of the epidemiology of the disease and the population characteristics of the study area.
the epidemiology of a given disease in a given setting is a critical determinant of the optimal study design.
the epidemiology of DENV is highly heterogeneous, both spatially and temporally, and that this must be accounted for in the design of future trials.
